=== SLIDE 3 ===
Architectural Current State Deployment Model Deployment Source and Transfer The application package is prepared and manually transferred to the Windows Server hosting IIS for deployment. IIS Configuration IIS is configured with application pools, SSL bindings, and environment-specific settings to host the application securely. Application Deployment and Validation The application is deployed to the designated IIS site, followed by validation of database connectivity. Smoke Testing Smoke tests are performed to verify that the deployed application functions correctly before going live.

=== SLIDE 5 ===
Data Journey As-Is 13/07/2026 13
=== SLIDE 6 ===
Data Journey As-Is High Level Data flow journey BSE System:  is used by Apha users ( authenticate through Windows Authentication)  to view and manage BSE case information. All case-related data is entered into the system manually. The system also provides administrators with functionality to maintain user roles, user account details, and reference data. The BSE system is also integrated with  SharePoint , enabling users to retrieve scanned case forms directly from the SharePoint repository. BSE Database:  is  SQL Server 2022 (hosted on DEFACPVWPSQL002) and  the central repository for all  BSE case related data.  It contains several key data domains: BSE case details Roles and User’s data Reference and lookup data Data Integration:  There are 2 SQL Server Integration (SSIS) packages: BSESS Import Package  pulls surveillance data from the TSE database into the BSE system.  The TSE Database provides additional data such as Animal records, Laboratory samples, Testing group and Laboratory result code.  BSE Access Export  package extracts data from core BSE Database tables and populates four dedicated export tables within the same database. These tables are consumed by MS Access users to view Herd Sizes, Cases, Farms, and Relations data. Data Access:  Users connect to BSE Database to retrieve data for Business Intelligence (BI) reporting through:  MS Access SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
=== SLIDE 7 ===
Architectural To-Be 13/07/2026 15
=== SLIDE 8 ===
# Decision Area Design Consideration  Decision Rationale DD001 Hosting Adherence to cloud first strategy. The use of CDP and other containerisation platforms considered vs the use of a PaaS service. Use Azure Container Apps with Linux containers for hosting the modernised .NET 10 application. – CDP not deemed appropriate due to additional effort. Azure Container Apps is a serverless container platform built on Kubernetes Linux containers provide portability, environment consistency, and cloud-native scalability aligned with Defra’s  modernisation  strategy. CDP  does not support SQL Server. Currently it supports MongoDB, hence the use of CDP discounted. DD002 Database The use of CDP supported DB services-MongoDB  or other DB services vs the use of a Azure SQL Database The strategic direction is to use PostgreSQL where viable. Use the  Azure SQL Database . Azure SQL Database integrate seamlessly with .NET development tools (ADO.NET, Entity Framework, Azure DevOps).   The application currently uses an MS SQL DB and c hoosing Azure SQL over alternative database platforms avoids the significant redevelopment effort DD003 Monitoring and Alerting The use of other monitoring &amp; alerting services vs the use of Azure App Insights Azure Application Insights provides first-class support for .NET 10 containerised applications deployed in Azure Container Apps Azure Application Insights automatic provide dependency tracking and distributed tracing. Seamless integration with Azure Monitor and Log Analytics, providing lower configuration overhead. 16 Design Decisions
=== SLIDE 9 ===
Architecture Future State High Level To-Be: Logical System Architecture
=== SLIDE 10 ===
Architecture Future State High Level To-Be: Cloud Architecture with Hub-Spoke pattern 18 1. User Access User Traffic enters the environment through the Hub, where the Azure Firewall and Private DNS provide secure routing and name resolution. This ensures all inbound and outbound flows are centrally governed before reaching spoke resources. 2. Hub &amp; Spoke Connectivity VNET peering enables secure communication with the hub and database spoke while maintaining isolation. The BSE containerised application (.NET 10, Linux containers) and supporting services operate within the spoke network, protected by NSGs and integrated with Azure Entra ID, Key Vault, and App Insights. 3. Database Tier  The BSE SQL Database is hosted in a dedicated spoke, exposed only through private IP and controlled via granular NSG rules. This tier stores all application data and provides secure, high‑performance connectivity to the application tier. 4. Data Synchronisation via ADF Azure Data Factory performs scheduled data preparation and synchronization tasks, connecting securely to the Azure SQL database through Private Endpoints, while connectivity to the external on‑premises database is routed securely via the hub through the Fortinet appliance . 5. External Connectivity manually  user system Data Analytics users connect to the BSE Database using SSMS from AVD with Read only access. Also, they connect to SharePoint by clicking the predefined link from BSE Portal

=== SLIDE 13 ===
Direct SQL Access Via AVD: DEFRA Secured-by-design principles Additional Security Controls for Direct SQL Access Via AVD Category Key Points Protective Monitoring All SQL logins and query executions are logged via SQL Auditing to Log Analytics, enabling full traceability. Azure Sentinel correlates read‑only user activity with identity logs to detect threats or abnormal access patterns. Defender for SQL monitors for suspicious or high‑risk behavior such as unusual data extraction, credential misuse, or query anomalies. Data Encryption &amp; Protection All SSMS connections to Azure SQL enforce TLS 1.2+ encryption in transit end‑to‑end. Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) secures all data at rest within the BSE database. Data Analytics users receive read‑only SQL roles ( db_datareader ) only, with no rights to modify data, objects, or schemas. MFA and Conditional Access policies help prevent unauthorized use of SSMS from unmanaged devices or locations. Isolation &amp; Lateral Movement Protection Category Key Points Isolation (Despite Direct Access) Data Analytics users connecting through SSMS from inside Azure Virtual desktop  are restricted to a single authorized Azure SQL database, preventing visibility of any other databases in the environment. Query execution is constrained to only the permitted database, ensuring users remain fully isolated from other workloads Lateral Movement Protection Database‑level permissions ensure users cannot list, browse, or connect to other SQL instances or datasets, stopping lateral movement within the data tier Access to master, model, msdb, and any neighboring databases is denied, preventing privilege escalation or unauthorized dataset access. Operations such as cross‑database queries, linked server connections, metadata inspection, or stored procedure enumeration are blocked by permissions. ● Monitoring ● Audit ● Access Control ● Data Protection

Database  Microsoft SQL Server 2022 Azure  SQL Database Aligned with Microsoft Tech Stack, and in-line with Defra’s approved technology. Principles Alignment 13/07/2026 27
=== SLIDE 21 ===
Enterprise Architecture Principles Alignment Link to Principles on Architecture SharePoint Site ,  SSL Accessible Principles Link Principle Detail How the Design Aligns to the Principle 1. Delivery-Focused Architecture Clear Scope and Time-Bound Objective :   The architecture is designed to enable modernisation of the legacy application to a cloud-native, containerised .NET 10 platform by Q3–Q4 2026, ensuring alignment with modernization goals. Iterative Discovery and Validation:  The approach includes iterative engagement with business SMEs, LAP teams, and Cognizant partners to validate assumptions and fill gaps in legacy knowledge. Governance Embedded:  The architecture is being developed in alignment with Defra’s SDA, TDA, and CTWG governance processes, with resources allocated to support approval and refinement. 2. Design for Users Business Analysis:  The design incorporates insights from current usage patterns of the BSE application, ensuring that user workflows are preserved while improving efficiency. Support for Testing and Validation:  The architecture introduces dedicated test environments, addressing the current limitation where validation occurs in production. Simplification of Data Journeys:  The solution aims to streamline manual processes and fragmented IIS configurations into a cloud-native, automated platform, reducing complexity for users. 3. Maximise Value, Minimise Waste Decommissioning of Legacy Components :  The migration removes reliance on Windows Server 2016, IIS 10, and manual configurations, reducing operational overhead and future licensing costs . Consolidation of Fragmented Solutions:  Current multiple IIS application pools and manual scripts will be consolidated into a single, maintainable architecture. Cloud-Native Design:  The proposed solution aligns with Defra’s Cloud Centre of Excellence (CCoE) strategy, enabling scalability, maintainability, and cost-effective hosting.
=== SLIDE 22 ===
Enterprise Architecture Principles Alignment Link to Principles on Architecture SharePoint Site ,  SSL Accessible Principles Link Principle Detail How the Design Aligns to the Principle 4. Clean Data, Clear Decisions Single Source of Truth :  The architecture will consolidate all application configurations and dependencies discovered during the discovery phase into a unified repository. Data Mapping:  Mapping will clarify which components are active, redundant, or require remediation, reducing unknown dependencies. Data Quality and Testing:  Plans include regression testing and validation of data flows to ensure accuracy and reliability post-migration. 5. Connect and Collaborate Landscape complexity:  The architecture acknowledges the complexity of the current environment, involving multiple stakeholders and legacy dependencies. Coordinated Governance and Approval:  Developed in alignment with Defra’s governance processes (SDA, TDA, CTWG), ensuring shared responsibility and transparency. Knowledge Consolidation:  Documentation from current IIS configurations and operational practices will be consolidated to create a single source of truth. 6. Secure Today, Safe Tomorrow Secure-by-Design:  The new architecture will embed security controls aligned with Defra’s approved security frameworks. Cloud-Native Security Architecture:  Designed to meet CCoE standards, ensuring scalability and resilience against evolving threats. Move to Aligned Technologies:  The move away from unsupported legacy technologies to modern, secure cloud-native services ensures the platform remains safe and supportable in the future.

Enterprise Architecture Principles Alignment Link to Principles on Architecture SharePoint Site ,  SSL Accessible Principles Link Principle Detail How the Design Aligns to the Principle 7. Empower to Innovate Removal of Legacy Constraints:  Eliminating manual IIS configurations and outdated OS creates space for automation and innovation. Supportability and Scalability:   The architecture is designed for maintainability and scalability, reducing technical debt for future teams. Foundations for Future Capability:  Moving to a  CCoE -managed platform enables integration with modern DevOps practices and future enhancements. 8. Right Tools, Right Place Strategic Platform:  The architecture will be aligned with Defra’s approved technologies and cloud design templates, ensuring platform suitability and long-term sustainability for the migrated application. Fit for Purpose Technology Stack:  The current system relies on Windows Server 2016 and IIS 10, with manual configurations and fragmented application pools. The new solution consolidates these into a cloud-native architecture appropriate to the scale and complexity of the service. DevOps Pipeline:   The architecture ensures that modern tools such as Azure DevOps, CI/CD workflows, and automated deployment pipelines are implemented across development, testing, and production stages, replacing manual processes and reducing operational risk.

Risks Ref Title Description RAG Impact Mitigation R-001 Direct Database Access via SSMS End users connecting directly to the production SQL Server environment using SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) via AVD in read-only mode, potentially bypassing application‑level controls and gaining access to sensitive data or executing unauthorized queries. Amber Medium Provide controlled reporting interfaces; implement audit logging; educate users on secure data access practices; review permissions periodically. R-002 Security vulnerabilities BSE system is often outdated and unpatched, making cloud transitions high‑risk if not secured. Red High Leverage cloud provider security features with identity hardening, zero‑trust control &amp; encryption

NFR - 002 Recovery Point Objective(RPO) They system must ensure that, in case of a failure, no more than 4 hours of data lost, in alignment with Tier 3 services levels. NFR - 003 Recovery Time Objective(RTO) The system must recover and be fully operational within 4 hours after a failure, as required under Tier 3 service levels. NFR – 004 Operational Hours The system must be fully available for end‑users during standard business hours, operating between 09:00 and 17:00 GMT/BST, Monday to Friday.  Non-Functional Requirements

=== SLIDE 34 ===
DEFRA seeks to exit from Civica-managed hosting and support arrangements by migrating and modernising seven critical Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) applications to secure, compliant, and sustainable Defra Cloud-based platforms. These legacy applications are currently distributed across Civica, Atos Datacentre, and hybrid configurations, and require remediation, rationalisation, and alignment with Defra’s cloud-first strategy and security standards.  We wish to undertake a project to move the solution towards alignment of the technologies and practices of the Defra Cloud Centre of Excellence ( CCoE ) definitions, demonstrating benefits against observed obsolescence, technical debt and security markers, without widespread implementation and significant business disruption. Introduction Background Current State  On-Prem VM  (current state) Target State Cloud-native solution in Defra CCoE platform (alignment to CCoE)

A5 – Service Design, GDS &amp; Compliance Summary 13/07/2026 42
=== SLIDE 38 ===
Service Design, GDS &amp; Compliance Summary Accessibility Compliance Statements ☐ The supplier must not introduce any new WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility regressions during the migration. ☐ The supplier must complete and provide results from WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility testing. ☐ The supplier must confirm that the existing accessibility statement remains accurate post‑migration. GOV.UK Design System Compliance Statements ☐ The supplier must ensure no changes are made to the UI that break current GOV.UK‑aligned behavior. ☐ The supplier must ensure the migrated platform remains technically ready for future GOV.UK Design System adoption in 2026. Privacy Compliance Statements ☐ The supplier must confirm no new personal data will be collected or processed as part of the migration. ☐ The supplier must confirm that encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and encryption at rest are fully implemented. ☐ The supplier must confirm the current DPIA remains valid and no new privacy risks have been introduced. Security Compliance Statements ☐ The supplier must ensure alignment with Defra Secure‑by‑Design controls. ☐ The supplier must configure Cloud KMS-managed encryption for all data stores. ☐ The supplier must ensure logging and monitoring is in place. GDS Compliance Statements ☐ The supplier must demonstrate alignment to each of the 14 points of the GDS Service Standard. ☐ The supplier must confirm no functional changes will be introduced during migration. ☐ The supplier must confirm that existing user journeys will be preserved until the 2026 rewrite.

=== SLIDE 42 ===
Introduction Objectives Obsolescence Removal of outdated, end-of-life, end-of-support components, with limited or diminishing intellectual knowledge and capability.  Technical Debt Removal of suboptimal technologies, and fragmented technology stacks that are not aligned to the Defra &amp;  CCoE  strategic direction. Security &amp; Compliance Remediation against known vulnerabilities, and enabling compliance to organisational security standards including remediation  The primary objective is to design and implement a modern solution for migrating and modernising hosted application within the Defra Azure tenancy, that is compliant with the Cloud Centre of Excellence (CCoE) patterns and standards. Address overengineering and complexity by standardising on unified and strategically aligned component framework whilst moving away from obsolete platforms and services and their associated licencing/maintenance costs. A secondary objective of this high-level solution architecture is to replicate the full current functional capability whilst enabling future scalability and enhancement opportunities. The design will ensure that existing service levels and resilience standards are maintained or improved on, supporting long-term operational efficiency and adaptability. Drivers The proposed solution will be planned to deliver benefits against observed obsolescence, technical debt and security markers, without widespread implementation leading to significant business disruption.
=== SLIDE 43 ===
Alignment to LAP Obsolescence Criteria Alignment to Architectural As-Is 6 Current Status Risk RAG Points Obsolescence ● Windows Server 2016 mainstream support ended on Jan 2022 with extended support till 2027.  IIS version 10 is approaching end‑of‑life ( i.e.- till Jan 2027)   with  limited vendor support. ASP.NET Web Forms (v4.0)  support ended by Jan 2016. Technical Debt ● There are no DevOps CI/CD practices in place. Server patching and maintenance are performed manually. Current path-to-live (TEST   Prod) is not aligned to DDTS standards. Security ● Inadequate security monitoring  (e.g.- Traffic Anomalies, File System Security Events) which is not aligned with Defra Secure by design principles No data encryption at rest as  SQL Server Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) is not  enabled. No data sharing protocol or data encryption enabled at transit (confirmed by Atos DBA) Application does not enforce HTTPS. Database Credentials are exposed in plain text in the codebase. Authentication &amp; Authorization flows are not following DEFRA standards. ● Red = High Risk ● Amber = Medium Risk ● Green = Low Risk
=== SLIDE 44 ===
Architectural As-Is 13/07/2026 7
=== SLIDE 45 ===
Architectural Current State Context Model  The current BSE(Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) system manages suspected and confirmed positive BSE cases under Active and Passive Surveillance workflows.  It supports RBSE allocation, case data entry, lab result updates,  and provides access (by redirecting) to scanned documents that are uploaded offline into  SharePoint  by APHA team members. The system also provides search, reporting, and audit logging to maintain compliance and traceability. BSE database pulls data from  TSE (Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies) system and uses it to compare with own bovine/cattle case data.
